Citi Corp Internship Interview Experience 
Sarang Shekokar 
Information Technology, 2018-22 
 
Due to the situation regarding COVID-19, all of our interviews for internship programs were being 
held online. The test and interviews for Citi were held on AMCAT platform.  
Online Test (2 hours): 
The online test for Citi was not restricted and was open for all branches. 
The online test consisted of 3 sections:  
●
Aptitude and Quants: Sums based on school level math were asked, topics such as 
fractions, work and time, etc. 
●
English Comprehension: There were short passages given and a few MCQ questions based 
on them were asked. 
●
Coding (60 mins, 2 questions): The coding round was fairly simple and not too difficult. 
Time required for solving also might have been a criteria. I was asked these 2 questions: 
1.
Given a number n, print the given pattern. 
Eg: For  n=5, 
 
 
 
 
2.
Given a number n, and matrix dimensions r,c. The first element in the matrix is n, 
and each subsequent element is incremented by 1. Multiply this matrix with its 
transpose and print the resultant matrix.  
Interview Round 1 (Technical): 
60 students were shortlisted for this round. Each candidate had a 20-minute interview call 
scheduled. 
The interview began with an introduction. The interviewer asked me to tell him about myself . He 
then asked me to explain to him all the various subjects I had had over the last 2 years. I was asked 
if I knew what was DBMS, which went something like: 
[INTERVIEWER]: So do you know what is DBMS? 
[ME]: Yes, DBMS stands for database management system.

[INTERVIEWER]: Okay tell me what is an index. 
[ME]: ………….. 
I did not know the answer to his question, but I just kept my calm. He then went on to the next 
question and asked me what is a Primary Key, which I could answer. 
After this he asked me about my favorite topic I studied in OS, my answer to which was 
Semaphores. He then asked me to explain semaphores and what was their use. 
Next he asked me which programming languages did I know, and then gave me a question to solve: 
“ Given an input, check if it is a palindrome”. I read the question twice to make sure if I had read the 
question correctly (Tip : ​however easy the question may sound please read it carefully​). I was asked to 
code it. 
He then asked me what Object Oriented Programming Language is and then asked me to explain 
Polymorphism and give a real world example of the same. 
Next, I was given another programming question. “Bob has a birthday party and his birthday cake 
is a rectangular fruit cake which is divided into smaller pieces of n rows and m columns, such that 
each piece has one specific fruit on it. He invites K friends over, who each have a favorite fruit. A 
friend is happy if he gets a piece of his favorite fruit. Maximize the number of friends who are 
happy.” I was just asked to explain my approach and logic for the problem, and not asked to code it. 
After these questions, he asked me if I had any questions for him (​always make sure you keep a 
couple of questions ready for this and ask something). 
In total I was asked about 5 theoretical questions and 2 coding questions​. 
Interview Round 2 (HR): 
About 30 students were shortlisted for this round. 
This interview was comparatively much more chill and laid back. The interviewer greeted me and 
asked me to tell him something about myself. I was then asked to explain what was my 
contribution in my previous internship and what was that project about (make sure you know 
what you’re putting in your resume because they do read it and ask questions accordingly) 
Next I was asked HR questions such as: 
●
Tell me about one difficult situation that you had to face and what did you learn from it. 
●
What are some of the qualities you look for in a leader, and who is one person, from any 
walk of life who you admire as a leader. 
●
Tell me about an instance where you have had differences with a fellow peer or colleague 
and how did you resolve it? 
●
Tell me two things that you have learnt during the lockdown period due to COVID. 
●
What are some of your interests other than studies? 
He then introduced himself, and explained what his position is at Citi. I was asked if I had any 
questions for him (​again ask something). ​He then thanked me for my time and said that we will be in 
contact with you soon.

The interviews went on for the whole day, and in the end, 12 candidates were selected. The 
interviews weren't too long and lasted for only 20 minutes. Always be prepared with topics such 
as DBMS, OOPS and OS along with DSA as questions can be asked on them.  
All the best! Always remember to stay positive, and agar first company mei nahi hua selection toh 
tension mat lo, aage aur bhi bohot aaenge. Just remember to stay calm and confident about the 
stuff that you know.  
Reach out to me at shekokarsarang@gmail.com for any queries.
